title: Update Jira Issue via Audio Upload
breadth_reason: This script tests the user's ability to update a Jira issue using uploaded audio, extending coverage beyond keyboard and live mic inputs.

v7_target.engine: User-device engine installed on the user's computer
v7_target.surface_rule: The user must have a signed-in Jira instance in their Chrome profile with an issue detail page open.
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof must be a screenshot of the Jira issue page showing the update after action, or a decline notice if surface unverifiable.

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio provides full ASR coverage for the spoken instruction, bypassing live mic uncertainty.

real_user_surfaces.name: Jira Issue Page
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible issue detail page with ANL-114 number and update field available.

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome Profile
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Anticipy can detect that the browser profile has Jira session cookies.

moments.description: User navigates to anticipy.ai/app and completes onboarding to download and install the user-device engine.
Anticipy checks that the user's Chrome profile has a signed-in Jira tab with an issue detail page open for ANL-114.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please update the Jira issue ANL-114 for the analytics repo with a comment that pytest is failing on the renewal test and tag it bug. If you cannot prove the visible Jira issue or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger must produce a new MP3 audio artifact per run using the say command, containing the exact spoken_reference_text.
moments.description: User uploads the MP3 audio file via /api/listen/upload. ASR transcribes the spoken instruction.
The engine checks that the transcribed text contains the Jira issue key ANL-114 and actionable phrases like 'update' and 'comment'.

acceptable_outcomes: act: Update the Jira issue ANL-114 with the comment and tag it as a bug.
ask: Request clarification if the Jira surface is ambiguous or incomplete.
decline: Refuse to update if the Jira issue page is not verifiable or the user is not signed in.
moments.description: The engine decides on the appropriate action based on the surface proof.
The driver observes that only the audio upload input mode is used; no live mic or paste alternatives are accepted for this test.

success_criteria: The user successfully uploads an MP3 audio file containing the spoken instruction.
Anticipy's ASR correctly transcribes the instruction and extracts the Jira issue key ANL-114.
If the user's Jira surface is verifiable, Anticipy updates the issue with the comment and tags it as a bug.
If the Jira surface is not verifiable, Anticipy declines with a clear message.
All actions are performed on the user's actual signed-in Chrome profile.
failure_triggers: The audio upload fails due to file format or size issues.
ASR misinterprets the spoken instruction, e.g., missing the issue key or action.
The Jira issue page is not visible or the user is not signed in.
Anticipy attempts to update Jira using a fake or cloned browser profile instead of the real one.
The proof provided is a stale screenshot or log from a previous session.
